samples.summary: New yorkie-doc-store tests are green on the unfixed code — every frontend change in this diff is type-annotation-only
samples.evidence: All three new tests ('an edit does not erase the caret lineAffinity from presence', 'undo restores the caret lineAffinity that was recorded', 'leaves a position with no affinity exactly as it was') are presented as pinning the #933 fix ("It was typed `{blockId, offset}`, which is how the wrap-boundary reading was documented as 'erased after each edit'"). But the only frontend changes in the diff are TypeScript annotations (`{blockId, offset}` → `DocPosition`) plus comments; at runtime `recordHistoryPresence` does `activeCursorPos: cursor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2950) and `setCursorForHistory` passes the caller's object straight through (2926-2927), so the `lineAffinity` property was never stripped. These tests therefore pass identically before and after the change and cannot fail for the defect their comments describe. They remain useful as guards against a future field-by-field rebuild, but they are not coverage of anything this diff changed.

samples.summary: The new `lineAffinity ?? position.lineAffinity` fallback in resolvePositionPixel is never exercised with an omitted param and a position that carries an affinity
samples.evidence: The JSDoc added by this change says "Omit it to use the affinity the position itself carries", but no test drives that combination. packages/docs/test/view/peer-cursor.test.ts (lines 88, 107, 130) always passes an explicit 'backward'. In the new editor-level test the peers pass `peer.position.lineAffinity`, which is either defined (so the param wins) or undefined together with the position (so the final `'backward'` default wins) — the middle clause `?? position.lineAffinity` is never the deciding one, so deleting it would keep every test green.

samples.summary: scrollToPosition switching from hardcoded 'backward' to pos.lineAffinity has no test
samples.evidence: The change makes `scrollToPosition` resolve pixels with `pos.lineAffinity` (editor.ts ~2841-2845), described as "a peer jumped to from the avatar list should land on the line their caret is on". Grepping packages/docs/test for `scrollToPosition` returns no hits at all (only `restoreLocalCursor` matches came back), and the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts does not call it. So this behavior change ships with no test that distinguishes it from the old hardcoded reading.

samples.summary: No test pins the precedence of moveTo's explicit affinity argument over the affinity carried by the position
samples.evidence: `moveTo` now resolves `affinity ?? pos.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'`. The new tests only cover the two ends: undo/redo restore passes a position with an affinity and no argument, and the ArrowRight/Home paths (text-editor.ts:2992, 3051) pass an explicit 'forward' with a freshly built position that carries no affinity. No test passes a position carrying one affinity together with the opposite explicit argument, so swapping the operands (`pos.lineAffinity ?? affinity`) would keep the suite green even though it would change which reading wins for callers like text-editor.ts:3832/3968/4005.

samples.summary: The lineAffinity setter path used by vertical motion is exercised but never asserted
samples.evidence: Vertical caret motion writes affinity through the new setter (`this.cursor.lineAffinity = result.lineAffinity`, text-editor.ts:4343/4379/4383/4412), and the setter is what this change altered to materialize the affinity onto `position`. The new tests press ArrowDown (lines 174, 200, 315) but only read `.offset` afterwards; affinity is asserted only after ArrowRight and after Home, both of which go through `moveTo(..., 'forward')` instead. So the setter-based publish for ArrowUp/ArrowDown (including the cross-page branch) is never asserted.
